title: Learning Where to Simulate: Generative Active Sampling for Online PDE Surrogate Training
claim: A closed loop couples simulation, surrogate training, and a generative sampler so new simulations target the hardest configurations.
layout: Single wide panel, numbered stages 1–4 in a loop, buffers as cylinders
description: One wide diagram of a four-stage online loop, with each stage marked by a purple numbered circle. At bottom left (1), solver runs S(λ_i) appear as colored boxes: finished in red, running in blue, waiting in gray. Dashed lines separate the three states, and a time arrow runs below. Blue arrows carry states X_t^λ into an orange cylinder buffer R. From R, a black arrow goes up and across to a rounded box labeled Deep Surrogate, which shows stacks of PDE field heatmaps on either side of a small neural net (2). The output goes to a second cylinder buffer B (3). Below B, an MLP discriminator splits into DDPM training and debiasing branches. At right, the Resampling panel (4) has a DDPM sampler and a mixture of generated and uniform λ distributions weighted by α. Gray curves return from this mixture to the waiting solvers, closing the loop.
caption: OGAS workflow. (1) Trajectory Streaming: Solvers, parametrized with different $\boldsymbol{\lambda}$, run concurrently and stream states $X_t^{\boldsymbol{\lambda}}$ into an in-memory buffer $\sR$. (2) Surrogate Update: The surrogate model trains on batches sampled from $\sR$ and computes per-sample difficulty signals $\tilde{\epsilon}$. (3) Generative Training: Pairs $(\boldsymbol{\lambda}, \tilde{\epsilon})$ are buffered in $\sB$ to train a conditional generative model in parallel with the surrogate. (4) Adaptive Sampling: The generative sampler draws new $\boldsymbol{\lambda}$ conditioned on high difficulty values $\tilde{\epsilon}$ to parametrize subsequent solver executions.
abstract: Paper published at NeurIPS 2026. For data-driven PDE surrogates, generalizing across a wide range of initial conditions and physical coefficients requires a training set of numerical simulations that consistently covers the resulting dynamics. Yet uniform sampling of these configuration parameters can leave challenging regimes insufficiently covered, leading to high prediction errors and large error variance in the trained surrogate. To address this sampling imbalance, we introduce the Online Generative Active Sampling (OGAS), which continuously adapts configuration sampling during surrogate training, as an alternative to classical round-based active learning. As the surrogate learns from a stream of simulation data generated online, OGAS trains a fast diffusion model in parallel to sample configuration parameters conditioned on a training difficulty signal, such as loss or uncertainty. This conditional sampler enables OGAS to parametrize subsequent simulations to generate challenging training data by prioritizing configurations with high difficulty values. We evaluate OGAS on 2D PDEs with distinct challenging dynamics-Kuramoto--Sivashinsky, Navier--Stokes, and Gray--Scott-using multiple surrogate architectures and up to 308 configuration parameters. Across the tested PDEs and architectures, OGAS consistently reduces the 99th-percentile prediction error and overall error dispersion compared with uniform sampling, while wall-clock overhead is negligible. Code and experiments are available at https://github.com/melissa-sa/ogas.
